headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: Devin’s broad workspace/OAuth access can collide with EMQX’s HTTP/API-facing broker role, while prompt-injection and cascading-error risks remain moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin ingests files, browser content, MCP outputs, and shared integrations by default, so malicious content from EMQX-managed messages or HTTP payloads could be treated as instructions. EMQX exposes HTTP API surfaces and handles IoT data, creating a plausible bridge. No direct provenance controls are documented for either agent, so uncertainty stays on the higher side.
conditions: IF Devin reads EMQX-originated content from a shared workspace, Slack thread, or MCP server without provenance tags, injection is plausible.
IF EMQX forwards attacker-controlled text into Devin’s browser or file inputs, Devin may follow embedded instructions.
mitigations: Restrict Devin to trusted, signed inputs only.
Add provenance labels to EMQX-fed messages before Devin reads them.
Disable MCP paths that carry untrusted text.
Use a separate review step for any EMQX-generated instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin has broad filesystem, browser, and integration access plus handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens; EMQX touches IoT data and exposes HTTP APIs. If they share a workspace or connected integration, sensitive data can flow from Devin’s context into EMQX-facing outputs or vice versa. The pair’s interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty is escalated but the default blast radius is still substantial.
conditions: IF Devin and EMQX share a workspace, repo, or API token, data can cross between them.
IF Devin processes files containing secrets or IoT payloads and EMQX receives derived outputs, leakage is possible.
mitigations: Separate credentials for Devin and EMQX.
Block secret-bearing files from Devin’s inputs.
Route EMQX data through a redaction step first.
Audit shared integrations for unintended data export.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin can write the filesystem, modify git state, and use broad network egress; EMQX exposes HTTP APIs and broad egress. That creates overlapping mutable surfaces if they operate on the same repo, ticket, or API-backed resource. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so conflicts are plausible in default collaborative setups.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or shared API resource, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF Devin commits while EMQX updates the same mutable record via HTTP, state divergence is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate branches or resource IDs.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Add a quick lock file or mutex in the shared workspace.
Review diffs before merge or publish.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can autonomously act inside its workspace and use integrations, while EMQX exposes HTTP APIs and handles IoT data. If EMQX consumes Devin’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or records. The pairwise handoff is inferred rather than directly evidenced, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF EMQX ingests Devin-generated text without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF Devin produces a malformed command that EMQX executes through HTTP automation, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require schema validation on Devin outputs.
Add human approval before EMQX acts on Devin text.
Compare Devin output against source data before execution.
Log and diff all handoff payloads.
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs, and requests Slack/Jira/Notion write scopes; EMQX touches IoT data. If regulated IoT or personal data is routed from EMQX into Devin’s third-party cloud workspace or integrations, retention and residency obligations may diverge. Only Devin’s compliance surface is documented, so the other side is cited via its data class and API exposure.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is sent from EMQX into Devin’s cloud workspace, residency or retention mismatches may arise.
IF Devin writes EMQX-derived data into Slack, Jira, or Notion, subject-rights handling may become inconsistent.
mitigations: Classify EMQX data before sending it to Devin.
Disable storage of regulated data in Slack/Jira/Notion.
Set short retention on shared artifacts.
Review vendor DPAs and residency settings.
requires-engineering: enforce compliance routing rules.
